clue.text: Top sheep ventured around well, bothering that female

indicators.note: the wager word goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: to venture money is to bet it

indicators.note: something bothered is ruffled and disturbed, so the letters of well are jumbled

parts.note: her refers to a woman already named

explanation.surface: A shepherd's wager about a well, with some woman bothering over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothering' looks like it governs 'that female' but signals the jumble of 'well'; 'around' puts the wager round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The wether wearing the bell leads the flock, so the word means the leading sheep, and by extension any trendsetter.

clue.text: Second in command calling back Mayor?

indicators.note: calling back means the occupation word is read backwards

parts.note: a calling is a vocation or job

indicators.note: the second letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A deputy recalling the mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: BOJO was a nickname for Boris Johnson, Mayor of London from 2008 to 2016; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname belonged to a politician who was then serving as London's Mayor, so he is an example.

clue.text: See Olympic track finals with fan. It creates tight security in building

definitions.text: It creates tight security in building

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see

indicators.note: the final letters of the two following words are taken

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, as in a sports nut

explanation.surface: Watching the Olympic track finals with a fan while the stadium has tight security.
explanation.definitionFit: A second nut tightened against the first stops it working loose, keeping a fastening secure in construction.

clue.text: Bill about tax reproduced on printer

parts.note: Bill is a familiar short form of William
C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: reproduced means made again in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bill about tax copied out on a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Caxton set up the first printing press in England in the fifteenth century, so he was a printer.

clue.text: Jungle inhabitant's extremities seen over in lake

indicators.note: the turned letters sit inside the lake word

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake

indicators.note: turned over means the alphabet's ends are read backwards

parts.note: A and Z are the extremities of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A jungle dweller's hands and feet are seen dangling in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremities' suggests limbs but means A and Z, the alphabet's ends; 'over' turns them to ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs's ape-man hero was raised in and lives in the African jungle.

clue.text: Close to game, poles and flag halted group of players

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles

indicators.note: halted means stopped short, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a flag is an emblem of a nation

explanation.surface: Near the end of a match, the posts and flag stopped a team.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble is a small group of musicians or actors who perform together.

clue.text: Current Poet Laureate?

definitions.meaning: a current is a flowing river, here one dividing Germany and Poland
someone who writes odes, a whimsical coinage hence the question mark

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is an invented word, one who makes odes, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a European river, and a river is a current of water; a writer of odes is jokingly a poet.

clue.text: God suppresses a number of Romans (10) scheming

indicators.note: the god word holds down the numbers inside it

parts.note: deus is Latin for god
V is the Roman numeral five
the letters I and O look like the digits 1 and 0

explanation.surface: A deity crushing ten Romans, plotting all the while.
explanation.walkthrough: '(10)' looks like a chapter or a letter count but is a visual pun: IO resembles 10.
explanation.definitionFit: Devious and scheming are synonyms describing someone who uses underhand, cunning methods.

clue.text: Shoot includes fashionable gear for high-flyer

indicators.note: the shoot word takes the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: a runner is a plant shoot that creeps along the ground

indicators.note: able to be fashioned, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A photo shoot featuring trendy clothes for a high achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: The gunner in a bomber's rear turret flew high in the aircraft, so humorously a high-flyer.

clue.text: Judge visual comic

parts.note: ocular means relating to the eyes and sight

explanation.surface: An order to assess a visual comedian, or a cartoon strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something funny or playful, so they are synonyms as adjectives.

clue.text: Guitarist to work with sextet in the main

indicators.note: the working sextet sits inside the main

parts.note: the main is an old poetic term for the open sea
to go is to function or work, as a machine does
VI is the Roman numeral six, a group of six

explanation.surface: A guitarist joining a six-piece group to perform at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrés Segovia was the celebrated Spanish classical guitarist of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Commit to the task fully, having obtained axe, and scrape corner

parts.note: got means obtained
to hew is to chop with an axe
a hole is a tight spot or scrape
to hog something is to corner or monopolise it

explanation.surface: A workman with a new axe scraping a corner, fully committed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something completely, holding nothing back.

clue.text: I'm no stranger to travel, involving the foremost of landings

definitions.text: I'm no stranger to travel, involving the foremost of landings

indicators.note: letters made to travel move about into a new order
the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An astronaut boasting of familiarity with journeys, landings included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' adds L (first of 'landings') to the letters of I'M NO STRANGER before they are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the moonwalker.
explanation.definitionFit: The first man on the Moon was certainly a seasoned traveller who knew all about a famous landing.

clue.text: Massive edition kept in stock, by all accounts

indicators.note: the size and edition letters are held inside the stock word

parts.note: a supply is a stock of goods
OS stands for outsize

explanation.surface: A huge print run of a book is held in the warehouse, reportedly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean according to what is generally said or believed.

clue.text: When computer operating, university training engrosses Berners-Lee

indicators.note: to engross is to absorb, so the training word takes in the name

parts.note: PE is physical education, school training
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web

explanation.surface: A university course that has Tim Berners-Lee absorbed in his work.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) is a common British school abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptime is the period a computer system is running and available, as opposed to downtime.

clue.text: Disrobes when retired, and showing sloth perhaps, wakes up late

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for disrobes is read backwards

parts.note: someone who peels strips off their clothes
sloth is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: Someone undresses for bed and then, slothful, oversleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like going to bed, which suits the surface, but it signals the backwards reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in bed past the usual time is an idiom for rising late in the morning.

clue.text: Plant pine during perfect morning, when retired

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, so the assembled letters are read backwards
the yearning word sits within the pair of words for perfect and morning

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
AM is short for ante meridiem, the morning
to pine is to long for something

explanation.surface: Planting a pine one fine morning, then going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written with the letter I for the digit; 'when retired' looks like going to bed but turns the whole assembly round.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnolia is a flowering tree or shrub, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Toil persistently twisting neck abroad

indicators.note: a word twisted round faces the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: to neck a drink is to gulp it down
away means out of the country, abroad

explanation.surface: Someone abroad twisting their neck, as a weary tourist might.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to keep working steadily at something tedious.

clue.text: A French game — not one that's different

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a

indicators.note: one is I, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: quail is a game bird

explanation.surface: A French sport, though not one that is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Unequal things differ in size, amount or value, so they are different.

clue.text: Accident truncated part of church

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter of the church word is removed

parts.note: the chancel is the area around the altar of a church

explanation.surface: A mishap that left part of a church shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something happening by luck rather than design, as in by accident.

clue.text: Short letter, showing temperature during Christmas vacation in Egypt

indicators.note: the temperature letter sits within the festive word

parts.note: Noel is another word for Christmas

indicators.note: vacating a word empties its middle, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A brief note about the weather while holidaying in Egypt at Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' reads as a holiday but means emptying EGYPT to E and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A notelet is a small folded sheet of notepaper for brief messages.

clue.text: Bird eats chop and banger

indicators.note: the bird word takes the chopping word inside it

parts.note: the jay is a bird of the crow family
to lop is to chop off

explanation.surface: A bird dining on a pork chop and a sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banger' looks like a British sausage, matching the chop, but it is also British slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is British slang for a decrepit old car, and a jalopy is the same thing.

clue.text: English town centre to support heavyweight after he's thrown hammer

indicators.note: the central letter and the weight follow the jumbled letters
thrown means upset and confused, so the letters are jumbled
the middle letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a ton is a very heavy weight
a mallet is a wooden hammer

explanation.surface: An athletic scene: a hammer thrower beside a burly heavyweight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' turns HE'S into SHE. SHEPTON MALLET is a small market town in Somerset, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a market town in Somerset, so it is an example of an English town.

clue.text: Referee carries this out to pitch

definitions.meaning: before a match the official flips a coin to decide ends
to pitch is to throw, or to be thrown about as a ship is

explanation.definitionFit: A coin flip starts many matches, and to throw or lurch about is the same verb.

clue.text: Laid back guards reportedly get income daily

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the sound-alike inside it
laid back, read the other way round, signals a reversal

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so a word that sounds like earn is used

parts.note: to earn is to get income from work

explanation.surface: Relaxed security guards collecting their pay every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid back' looks like an idiom for relaxed, but it gives DIAL; 'reportedly' makes URN from EARN, which DIAL guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Diurnal is a formal synonym meaning occurring each day, or active in the daytime.

clue.text: Old misery comes inside to play

indicators.note: the misery word goes inside the little word to

parts.note: hell is a state of great misery

explanation.surface: An old, miserable person comes indoors to play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy of the Moor of Venice is the play named here.

clue.text: University's stern with booze — this one?

definitions.text: University's stern with booze — this one?

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a boat, so the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: ale is a type of alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A university reproached for its strictness about drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: this one is the American university the wordplay builds.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League institution in New Haven, Connecticut is a famous university that fits the description.

clue.text: Sit angrily, preparing complaint

indicators.note: preparing means working the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sits in a temper while drafting a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' reads as a grievance but means an illness here.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and inflammation of the voice box is one such illness.
